items.title: FPI selling crosses Rs 52,000 crore in October as Nifty defies foreign exodus
items.text: Foreign portfolio investors pulled out over Rs 52,000 crore from Indian equities in October, surpassing September outflows. Despite persistent FPI selling driven by rising US Treasury yields and elevated crude oil prices, benchmark indices Nifty and Sensex rebounded sharply, supported by robust domestic institutional buying and IT sector gains.
items.summary: Foreign portfolio investors withdrew over Rs 52,000 crore from Indian equities in October, exceeding September outflows. Despite this selling due to higher US Treasury yields and crude oil prices, the Nifty and Sensex rebounded sharply. The rebound was backed by strong domestic institutional buying and gains in IT stocks.
items.title_hi: FPI बिक्री अक्टूबर में Rs 52,000 करोड़ पार कर गई, जबकि Nifty विदेशी निकासी का सामना करती रही
items.summary_hi: विदेशी पोर्टफोलियो निवेशकों ने अक्टूबर में भारतीय शेयरों से Rs 52,000 करोड़ निकाल लिए, जिससे सितंबर की निकासी भी अधिक हो गई। यूएस ट्रेजरी yields में वृद्धि और कच्चे तेल की ऊँची कीमतों के चलते निरंतर बिक्री के बावजूद, निफ्टी और सेंसेक्स तेजी से rebound किया, क्योंकि घरेलू संस्थागत खरीद और आईटी क्षेत्र में लाभ रहा।

items.title: Opposition's 'low-level acts' reinforce need for PM Modi's leadership: Kangana Ranaut
items.text: BJP MP Kangana Ranaut on Sunday criticised Opposition parties over calls for regime change, saying their actions reinforce the need for Prime Minister Narendra Modi's strong leadership. Citing unrest in France and global conflicts, she also condoled the deaths of 19 people in a stampede at a Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata.
items.summary: Kangana Ranaut criticised Opposition parties for calling for regime change and said their actions show the need for PM Narendra Modi's strong leadership. She cited unrest in France and global conflicts, and expressed condolence for the 19 people who died in a stampede at a Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata.

items.title: Jefferies’ Chris Wood says it’s time to diversify beyond AI. Where should investors look now?
items.text: Jefferies’ Chris Wood is urging investors to diversify beyond AI as earnings growth for global AI stocks is expected to slow sharply and valuations remain elevated. His Asia portfolio retains exposure to semiconductor companies while avoiding heavy AI capex spenders, with India, China and other Asian markets featuring prominently in the allocation.
items.summary: Jefferies analyst Chris Wood advises investors to move beyond AI because AI earnings growth is expected to slow and valuations stay high. His Asia portfolio keeps holdings in semiconductor firms while avoiding companies with large AI capital spending, focusing on India, China and other Asian markets.

items.title: Earnings, crude oil, Jio IPO key monitorables for investors next week
items.text: Quarterly earnings, crude oil, Jio Platforms' initial public offering and trading activity of foreign investors will drive investors' sentiment in a holiday-shortened week ahead, analysts said. Besides, developments in West Asia and the rupee-dollar trend would be tracked by investors. "Indian equities enter the coming week with improved momentum following two consecutive weekly advances and a strong recovery led by information technology stocks. items.title: FPIs pull out Rs 52,100 cr from equities in Oct so far amid global headwinds
items.text: Foreign portfolio investors have withdrawn Rs 52,100 crore from Indian equities as of October this year. This follows a net withdrawal of Rs 35,861 crore in September, indicating ongoing financial retreat. Elevated crude oil prices, higher US bond yields, and a stronger dollar have affected investor sentiment. Despite temporary buying by foreign investors on October 16, selling in certain sectors continues.

Higher crude oil prices, rising US bond yields, a stronger dollar, and continued sector‑wise selling have affected sentiment, despite some buying on October 16.

items.text: Braj Mohan Ram was sworn in as the 28th Governor of Odisha during a ceremony at Lok Bhavan. The oath of office was administered by Chief Justice Harish Tondon in the presence of notable dignitaries. Ram is a three-time Lok Sabha Member of Parliament from Jharkhand's Palamu district. He succeeds Hari Babu Kambhampati, who held the position before him. Ram was appointed by President Droupadi Murmu on October 12.

The cumulative outflow for 2026 reached ₹3.12 lakh crore, exceeding the earlier ₹1.66 lakh crore.

items.title: Indian refiners' fuel exports to West rise 43% amid Russian crude use
items.text: Refineries in India and two other countries that run on Russian crude shipped 1 billion euros (USD 1.2 billion) of oil products to sanctioning countries in September, up 43 per cent from August, according to the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA). Reliance Industries Ltd's Jamnagar refinery in Gujarat supplied six of the seven cargoes unloaded at EU ports that month, despite the bloc's ban on fuel made from Russian crude. The CREA report covers refineries in India, Turkiye and Brunei. The EU took 667 million euros' worth of their products, Australia 168 million euros, the US 15
items.summary: Indian refiners and those in two other countries using Russian crude exported oil products worth 1 billion euros to sanctioning countries in September, a 43% increase from August. Reliance Industries' Jamnagar refinery supplied six of the seven cargoes unloaded at EU ports that month, despite the EU ban on fuel made from Russian crude. The EU accounted for 667 million euros of the imports, while Australia and the US took 168 million and 15 million euros respectively.

items.title: India’s soybean output seen falling 2.1% to 107.93 lakh tonnes in Kharif 2026: Farmers' body
items.text: India's soybean production forecast indicates a slight decline to 107.93 lakh tonnes during the ongoing Kharif season. Drought-like conditions in Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Telangana are contributing to this reduction in output. However, increased production in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan is expected to compensate for these losses. The area cultivated with soybean increased by approximately 5 lakh hectares compared to the previous season.
items.summary: India's soybean output is expected to fall by 2.1% to 107.93 lakh tonnes in the Kharif 2026 season. Drought-like conditions in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Telangana are contributing to this decline, while higher output in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan may offset the loss. The soybean-sown area has risen by about 5 lakh hectares compared with the previous season.

items.title: India notifies first tariff cuts under New Zealand FTA
items.text: India will implement duty concessions for certain imports from New Zealand starting October 20, under a new FTA. The concessions include zero basic customs duty for sheep meat and specific rates for fish and wine. Additionally, provisions have been made for manuka honey and kiwi fruit imports with varying duties. Sensitive categories like dairy products are excluded from this trade liberalization agreement.

items.title: Delhi sets up DITI on lines of NITI Aayog, to act as premier advisory body
items.text: Delhi government has set up Delhi Institute for Transformation and Innovation (DITI) on the lines of NITI Aayog, for policy-making under its goal of "Viksit Dilli by 2047", officials said on Saturday. DITI will function as the Delhi government's premier advisory body for public policy, development strategy and institutional reforms, an official notification said. DITI replaces the Dialogue and Development Commission (DDC) that previously served as the think tank of the city government under AAP rule. Chief Minister Rekha Gupta had announced the constitution of DITI in Delhi's budget presented

items.summary: India is expected to keep importing Russian crude at close to current levels after US President Donald Trump waived sanctions and tariffs under a new law. Trump issued an executive order late on Friday waiving the sanctions, restrictions and duties of the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, a day before a 30‑day deadline expired. He had signed the law on September 18, which allows up to 100 per cent tariffs on goods from the five largest importers of Russian crude and gas.

items.title: Trump's sanctions waiver offers India temporary relief, no certainty: GTRI
items.text: US President Donald Trump's waiver from sanctions, restrictions and tariffs under the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act (SRIA) gives India temporary relief but offers no lasting certainty, and New Delhi should safeguard its energy security and buy oil on commercial terms, think tank GTRI said on Saturday. It said that the move gives India relief from threatened additional duties of up to 100 per cent linked to Russian oil purchases. "But the relief is reversible. Washington can restore the tariffs anytime, leaving India and other buyers uncertain about future US action," the Global Trade Researc
items.summary: US President Donald Trump's waiver under the SRIA provides India temporary relief from sanctions but no lasting certainty. The waiver relieves India from potential extra duties of up to 100% on Russian oil purchases, though the relief can be reversed. GTRI said New Delhi should protect its energy security and purchase oil on commercial terms.
items.title_hi: ट्रंप का sanctions waiver India को temporary relief देता है, no certainty: GTRI
items.summary_hi: US President Donald Trump's waiver under the SRIA भारत को अस्थायी राहत देता है लेकिन कोई स्थायी निश्चितता नहीं देता। इस छूट से भारत को रूसी तेल खरीद पर लगी अतिरिक्त शुल्क में up to 100% की राहत मिलती है, हालांकि यह राहत वापस ली जा सकती है। GTRI ने कहा कि नई दिल्ली को अपनी ऊर्जा सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित करनी चाहिए और तेल वाणिज्यिक शर्तों पर खरीदना चाहिए।
